title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text: A card on bb for a developer who wants Claude Code or Codex to run on a timer. Everything on this page is read, not run: the hub has not started a bb schedule. Read the stage table and the permission default first. Other places a schedule can live are compared in [Run it on a schedule with an approval step](../cheatsheets/schedule-with-approval.md).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text: bb is a local server and app that runs Claude Code, Codex and other agent CLIs as threads ([bb]). Its builtin automations plugin fires an agent prompt or a stored script on a 5-field cron with a timezone, or once at a set time or delay ([bb]).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text:
| Pipeline stage | bb feature |
|---|---|
| Fire on a timer | Automations: recurring cron or one-shot time or delay ([bb]) |
| Agent step | An agent automation that runs Claude Code or Codex ([bb]) |
| Script step (your render or upload script) | A stored script automation ([bb script runtime]) |
| Overlapping tick | "An automation has at most one active run." ([bb script runtime]) |
| Failed run | Retries after 30 seconds and then 60 seconds, never past the next scheduled run ([bb script runtime]) |
| Run history, pause, re-run | Run history and a sidebar to pause or re-run ([bb]) |
| Ask a person a question | Ask User Question card, open 30 minutes by default ([bb configuration]) |
| Generate video, images or audio | No bb feature |
| Approval gate before publish | No bb feature ([bb]) |
| Post to a platform | No bb feature |

"No bb feature" means none of the four bb records names one; the tool record lists orchestration as its only lever ([bb]). A failing run never pauses the automation ([bb script runtime]). A process that starts its own session, such as `tmux`, `setsid` or a daemon, is not stopped by bb ([bb script runtime]), so a long render launched that way is not cleaned up.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text:
The schedule flags, quoted from bb's automations skill ([bb], as quoted on 2026-11-12):

```text
--cron <expr>                  Recurring 5-field cron expression
--timezone <tz>                IANA timezone for --cron
--at <datetime>                One-shot run time, preferably ISO 8601
--in <duration>                One-shot delay, e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d
```

The full create command is not quoted in the record. Read `plugins/automations/skills/automations/references/creation.md`, the source named on the [bb] record.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text: The bb server machine, awake. bb's guide says: "while the server machine is asleep or off, nothing can reach bb and running threads may stop" ([bb multiple devices]). The Keep Awake plugin runs caffeinate, but a closed laptop lid still sleeps ([bb]). All state, including automations, lives under `~/.bb/` by default ([bb configuration]).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text:
The default when no mode is given, quoted ([bb]):

> When `--permission-mode` is omitted, the plugin chooses Approve for me (`auto`) when the provider supports it and otherwise uses Full Access (`full`).

In Full Access, the Claude Code provider setting `fullAccessApprovalsEnabled` defaults to false, and the docs say "`false` approves every request" ([bb configuration]). Set to true, it shows Claude Code's own `permissions.ask` rules, PreToolUse hooks that answer `ask`, and built-in safety checks ([bb configuration]). The records quote no other permission-mode values.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text:
What exists:

- An agent can ask a person through the Ask User Question card, which stays open 30 minutes by default; a server restart closes every open question ([bb configuration]).
- A person can pause or re-run an automation from the sidebar ([bb]).

What does not:

- Automations have no approval step of their own ([bb]).
- The records do not say whether an automation run can raise an Ask User Question card.

A gate before publish has to come from elsewhere; options are in [Run it on a schedule with an approval step](../cheatsheets/schedule-with-approval.md).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text:
- Plugins are full-trust code inside the server process and keep secret settings under `<dataDir>/plugins/<id>/secrets/` ([bb configuration]).
- The script runtime injects `BB_SERVER_URL` and IDs, not secrets ([bb script runtime]).
- A code read recorded on the tool record shows variables passed with `--env-json` kept as a string map in the plugin's SQLite file, so API keys do not belong there; the docs do not say this ([bb]).
- Binding the server to 0.0.0.0 exposes an API that, in the docs' words, "is unauthenticated and permits command execution and file reads" ([bb configuration]). Keep it on 127.0.0.1 and use bb connect or Tailscale Serve for phone access ([bb configuration]).
- Telemetry, quoted: "Production runs (the desktop app, `npx bb-app`, and `pnpm start` checkouts) send anonymous usage telemetry" ([bb]). The record states that `BB_TELEMETRY=false` turns it off and that it goes to PostHog ([bb]). The saved quote stops before the opt-out sentence, so the opt-out is the record's paraphrase, not a verbatim quote.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
What the hub did not find
text:
- No independent report of bb used outside coding. Every bb source in the hub is bb's own documentation, marked single-source ([bb configuration], [bb script runtime], [bb multiple devices]).
- Missed-tick behaviour after sleep: not confirmed by the docs. The tool record's fit notes say a code read suggests missed ticks collapse into one run, and that no doc states it ([bb]).

text:
No record holds an M3 Max timing for any model. Wan and mlx-video publish no Mac timing ([Wan 2.2], [mlx-video]). For MiniMax H3 the one published timing is minutes per denoising step on a larger machine ([MiniMax H3]). Mac figures that do exist are for other chips: about 1.5 s per step on an M5 Max ([Qwen-Image]) and 7.0 s per step on an M4 Pro ([FLUX 3 Image Klein]). The hub's one M3 Max run was a code renderer, run here once ([worked example](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/README.md)). M3 Max timings are a gap the hub intends to measure.

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text:
A table of platform rules for a developer who posts their own clips through official APIs. All of it is read, not run: the hub has posted nothing. Read the table, then the TikTok and YouTube sections. Every cell is from the record linked in its row unless the cell links another, as quoted on 2026-11-12; "not stated" means not stated in the record. Policy pages change without notice.

| Platform | Public posting without audit or review? | Daily or rate limit | AI disclosure rule | Monetisation rule on AI or mass-produced content | Price of posting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube ([YT revisions], [YT insert]) | Yes since 2026-11-02; default privacy is public | "100 videos.insert calls" per day per project | Disclose realistic AI content ([YT disclosure]); API flag `status.containsSyntheticMedia` | Not "mass-produced, generic, repetitive, or manipulative" ([YT monetisation]) | No cost stated |
| TikTok ([TT guidelines], [TT direct post]) | No: unaudited posts are private-only | "typically around 15 posts per day/ creator account"; init 6 requests per minute per token | Label realistic AI content ([TT community]); API flag `is_aigc` | Not stated | Not stated |
| Instagram ([IG publishing]) | Not stated; app review for Advanced Access not read | "100 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period" | `is_ai_generated` on the media container | Not stated | Not stated |
| Facebook Reels ([FB reels]) | Not stated; posts to a Page, not a profile | "30 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period" | `is_ai_generated`, defaults to false | Primarily unoriginal accounts "may see their account deemed non-recommendable and demonetized" ([Meta originality]) | Not stated |
| Threads ([Threads posts]) | Not stated; app review not read | "250 published posts within a 24-hour period" | `is_made_with_ai`; false "does not prevent automatic AI labeling" | Not stated | Not stated |
| X ([X pricing], [X automation]) | Not stated; automated posts allowed "for entertainment, informational, or novelty purposes" | Not stated | No label required or offered ([X authenticity]) | No monetisation rule; "duplicative or substantially similar posts" banned | "$0.015 per request", "$0.200" with a URL |
| LinkedIn ([LinkedIn share]) | Own profile: add the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product | No daily limit found | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Bluesky ([Bluesky video]) | No audit mentioned; verified email needed | A daily video-post limit exists; number not on the page | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Mastodon ([Mastodon posting]) | No app review; own-account token | Rate limits not read | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text: TikTok's guidelines say: "all content uploaded via this endpoint will be restricted to private viewing mode. To lift this restriction, your API client must undergo an audit" ([TT guidelines]). The audit's intended-use list then rejects the one-developer case: "Not acceptable: A utility tool to help upload contents to the account(s) you or your team manages." ([TT guidelines]). An unaudited client is also blocked unless the account itself is private ([TT direct post]). Posts can be made public later by hand in the app ([TT guidelines]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text: The revision history says: "Videos uploaded through the videos.insert method from unverified API projects are no longer restricted to private viewing mode." ([YT revisions]). It adds: "If you don't specify a value for the status.privacyStatus property in a videos.insert request, the uploaded video's privacy status defaults to public." ([YT revisions]). A test upload therefore needs `status.privacyStatus` set explicitly.

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text:
- Instagram: the guide quotes 100 API posts per 24 hours in its rate-limit section, and the record notes 50 published posts per 24 hours in the carousel section; the record advises planning for 50 ([IG publishing]).
- LinkedIn: the Videos API gives "Between 75kb and 500MB", and the record notes the same page also states 5 GB ([LinkedIn share]).
- YouTube: the July 28, 2020 private-only rule is still on the same revision page; the 2026-11-02 entry reverses it ([YT revisions]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text: A C2PA manifest is "digitally signed by a trusted implementation" ([C2PA]). YouTube says content "containing C2PA metadata" gets a label the creator "can not" adjust ([YT disclosure]). YouTube is the only platform record found that states it reads C2PA ([C2PA]). On Threads, leaving `is_made_with_ai` false does not prevent automatic AI labelling ([Threads posts]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text:
- [Postiz]: self-hosting means "You create your own developer apps on each platform and go through their approval"; the self-hosted edition is AGPL-3.0. A self-hosted TikTok app hits the same audit wall ([TT guidelines]).
- [Mixpost]: Lite publishes to Facebook Pages, Mastodon and X; other platforms need Pro, "$299" one-time, as quoted on 2026-11-12.

| [n8n] | Schedule triggers (docs not read) | Docker or Node on a machine that stays on | Workflow pauses and sends a request via Slack, Telegram or n8n Chat | Sustainable Use License | On; `N8N_DIAGNOSTICS_ENABLED=false` |
| [Windmill] | Not stated in the record | Not stated in the record | Approval step suspends the flow; holders of secret URLs approve | Community Edition not for resale or managed service | Not read |
| [Trigger.dev] | Declarative schedules on the task, synced on dev or deploy | Self-hosted: a waiting run holds its resources | Waitpoint tokens | Apache-2.0, collected; checkpoints are Cloud-only | Not checked |
| [Temporal] | Calendar or interval specs | Temporal server plus your workers | No approval primitive; write a signal handler | MIT, collected; not quoted | Not checked |
| [Activepieces] | Not read | Not stated in the record | Flow Approvals reviews flow changes, not a run step | Flow Approvals is Enterprise or Cloud | Product analytics and a daily snapshot on |

title: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
heading_path: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
A pipeline with a gate before publish
text:
1. The schedule fires: [bb], [Hermes Agent], [cloud tasks][CC routines] or the [GitHub Actions schedule].
2. The agent writes and renders the clip: [claude -p] or [codex exec]. The renderer is your choice; the [worked example](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/README.md) was run here once.
3. Measure the file. Your own script; the example's `measure.py` is one model of it.
4. Stop for a person: required reviewers ([GitHub environments]), [n8n], [Windmill], [Trigger.dev] waitpoints, or a paused [Hermes Agent] job.
5. Publish with the platform's official API. Your own script; platform rules are in [publishing rules](publishing-rules.md).
6. Log what was posted. Your own script.

On GitHub, an environment secret stays locked until a required reviewer approves the job ([GitHub environments]), so the publish key can sit behind step 4.

title: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
heading_path: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
text:
- Claude Code `/loop`: "Recurring tasks automatically expire 7 days after creation." and "No catch-up for missed fires." ([CC scheduled tasks])
- Claude Code cloud tasks: "Expressions that run more often than once per hour are rejected." ([CC routines])
- GitHub Actions: "The shortest interval you can run scheduled workflows is once every 5 minutes." In a public repository a schedule is disabled after 60 days without activity, and "some queued jobs may be dropped" under load ([GitHub Actions schedule]).
- GitHub approval: "If you are on a GitHub Free, GitHub Pro, or GitHub Team plan, required reviewers are only available for public repositories." ([GitHub environments])
- n8n: "You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use." ([n8n])
- Windmill Community Edition: "not to sell, resell, serve as a managed service, modify or wrap under any form without an explicit agreement." ([Windmill])
- Hermes Agent: a missed occurrence runs late only inside a catch-up window of half the period, clamped to 2 minutes to 2 hours ([Hermes Agent]).
- Temporal: the default catch-up window is one year ([Temporal]).

title: Fact-check results
text:
What this is: the measured error rate of the hub's records, for anyone deciding how much to
rely on them. Read the summary, then the table, then the caveats.

All numbers on this page come from [evals/factcheck/2026-11-12.json](../evals/factcheck/2026-11-12.json).

title: Fact-check results
text:
On 2026-11-12 a different agent tool from the ones that wrote the records compared
112 records with the saved copies of their sources.

- **Quotes: 296 of 296 are verbatim.**
- **Claims: 39 of 296 (13.2%) said more than the source.**
  38 were overstated: a dropped condition, a wider scope. 1 was wrong.
- **Prose** (summaries and fit notes): 1504 statements. 74 overstated,
  22 not in the saved source, 4 wrong. 311 could not be
  checked from the saved source and are not counted as errors.
- **Category fields: 17 of 216 were not backed by the saved source.**

No invented quote and no wrong number was found in a quote. The typical fault is a true
sentence with its limiting clause removed.

title: Fact-check results
text:
- Checker: codex CLI. Writers: kiro CLI for most lanes, the driver agent for the first seven
  records. The checker got each record and the saved copy of its source, not the writer's notes.
- Unit: the atomic claim. Each got one verdict: supported, overstated, wrong, outdated, or
  not in source. Each quote was checked for being verbatim.
- First a seeded random sample: seed 20261112, 6 records per lane, 70 records,
  181 claims. Sample rate: 13.3%.
- Then every remaining record of the four lanes whose sample rate was over 15%.
- The checker did not open live pages. It judged each record against its own source.

text:
| Lane | Records checked | Claims | Not fully supported | Rate | Wrong | Prose findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| automation | 6 of 19 | 16 | 2 | 12.5% | 1 | 6 of 82 |
| contrarian | 11 of 11 | 30 | 5 | 16.7% | 0 | 16 of 142 |
| craft | 18 of 18 | 53 | 10 | 18.9% | 0 | 14 of 214 |
| footage-editing | 6 of 16 | 18 | 0 | 0.0% | 0 | 5 of 122 |
| hosted-models | 4 of 4 | 6 | 0 | 0.0% | 0 | 0 of 22 |
| hosted-models-2 | 6 of 17 | 14 | 2 | 14.3% | 0 | 7 of 79 |
| local-models | 6 of 15 | 17 | 1 | 5.9% | 0 | 1 of 81 |
| pipelines-research | 6 of 15 | 16 | 1 | 6.2% | 0 | 8 of 108 |
| publishing | 22 of 22 | 57 | 11 | 19.3% | 0 | 21 of 286 |
| quality-skills | 6 of 7 | 9 | 0 | 0.0% | 0 | 3 of 58 |
| quality-skills-2 | 6 of 12 | 16 | 2 | 12.5% | 0 | 6 of 95 |
| renderers | 15 of 15 | 44 | 5 | 11.4% | 0 | 13 of 215 |

Lanes checked in full: publishing, craft, contrarian, renderers. The other rows are samples
of 6 to 18 claims, so their rates are rough.

title: Fact-check results
text:
- First pass: 80 text edits in 50 records.
- Second pass: 35 text edits in 25 records. One finding was
  disputed by the fixer with the source line that supports the original text.
- No quote was changed in either pass.
- Category fields: 17 fields were not backed by the saved source. 2 were corrected (the saved source contradicted them). The rest are true values taken from another page of the same project and are left in place until each field carries its own quoted claim.
- Checked records carry `checked.by: agent:codex`.

title: Fact-check results
text:
- The three lanes still above 15% after a full check are the platform-rules lane, the craft
  standards lane and the "what failed" lane. Their records have been corrected, not re-verified.
- The corrections themselves were made by an agent and reviewed as a diff. They were not
  fact-checked a second time.
- The media-stages lane (audio and image stages) landed after the sample was drawn and is
  not checked.
- Records in the eight lanes under the line that were not sampled are unchecked. Expect about
  one claim in eight of those to overstate its source.
- "Not backed by the saved source" for a field means the one saved file does not show it.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
What this is: one controlled run per stack. For anyone choosing a code-driven renderer for a
coding agent. Read the verdict table, then "What the runs found", then the limits.

**Status: ran.** One run per arm on 2026-11-12. This is a tiny sample. It shows that both
stacks work end to end from the vendor's skills alone, and what each first deliverable looked
like. It does not rank the stacks.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
With only the vendor's own skills and one fixed [brief](BRIEF.md), does a Claude agent get a
spec-conformant 20 s clip out of each stack, locally, with no human help? What defects does
each first deliverable carry?

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
- Agent under test: one fresh Claude subagent per arm, given the brief and an empty folder.
- Skills: the ones each vendor ships. No other skills, no web search, no example repos.
- Machine: Apple M3 Max, 64 GB, macOS, Node 22, ffmpeg 7.1.1. Local render only.
- No human message during a run. A 30 minute cap.
- The pass or fail thresholds below were written down before either arm ran.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
An arm passes when its file is a readable MP4 at 1920x1080, 30 fps, 20.0 s +/- 0.5 s, h264,
has no black segment over 1.0 s after the first 0.5 s, no frozen segment over 4.0 s, and was
delivered inside the cap with no human message. [measure.py](measure.py) checks all but the
last two.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
Measured by `measure.py` on the delivered files (rung: agent-run for the clips, scripted-run
for the measurement). Files: [results/hyperframes.json](results/hyperframes.json),
[results/remotion.json](results/remotion.json).

| | HyperFrames | Remotion |
|---|---|---|
| Verdict against the threshold | pass | pass |
| Size, rate, length | 1920x1080, 30 fps, 600 frames, 20.0 s | 1920x1080, 30 fps, 600 frames, 20.0 s |
| Codec | h264, yuv420p | h264, yuv420p |
| File size | 780,393 bytes | 722,822 bytes |
| Black segments | 0.33 s at 2.97 s | 0.23 s at 0.0 s, 0.17 s at 7.93 s |
| Longest frozen segment | 2.17 s | 2.5 s |
| Share of the clip frozen | 0.716 | 0.544 |

From the agents' own run logs ([HyperFrames](results/hyperframes-runlog.md),
[Remotion](results/remotion-runlog.md)). These are self-reported, not measured by us:

| | HyperFrames | Remotion |
|---|---|---|
| Wall time | 7 min 46 s | 11.0 min |
| Full renders | 1 | 3 |
| Times the agent inspected frames | 3 | 4 |
| Fixes made after looking | 2 | 3 |
| Size of the working folder | 121M, plus 199M of cache outside it | 857M |

Clips: [results/hyperframes.mp4](results/hyperframes.mp4),
[results/remotion.mp4](results/remotion.mp4).
Contact sheets (12 frames each): [HyperFrames](results/hyperframes-sheet.png),
[Remotion](results/remotion-sheet.png).

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
Blind review (judgement, one reviewer, one clip per arm)
text:
A separate agent scored the two clips as "A" and "B" on six criteria, 0 to 2 each, from
stills. Full text with frame evidence: [results/review.md](results/review.md).

| Criterion | HyperFrames | Remotion |
|---|---|---|
| Copy exact | 1 | 1 |
| Hierarchy and type | 2 | 2 |
| Alignment and safe area | 2 | 2 |
| Palette obeyed | 1 | 2 |
| Entrances and transitions | 1 | 2 |
| Nothing clipped, overlapping or broken | 1 | 1 |
| Total out of 12 | 8 | 10 |

Why the two points differ, in the reviewer's words: the HyperFrames clip added a grey quote
panel and grey secondary text to the three briefed colours, and three of its scene changes
pass through a frame that shows only the accent bar. The Remotion clip's two dissolves stack
the outgoing and incoming headline for about five frames.

The reviewer could not judge easing or how the motion feels at speed. Nobody watched either
clip play.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
These are single observations from one run each.

- **Both install commands differ from the documentation.**
  - HyperFrames: `npx hyperframes skills update` starts a skills installer with `--global`
    that writes into the home directory's agent skill folders. The agent read that in the CLI
    source and did not run it. It used the skills bundled in the local npm package instead.
  - Remotion: `npx remotion skill` does not exist in 4.0.543. The command is
    `npx remotion skills add`, and it installs at project scope.
- **The HyperFrames CLI wrote outside the project**: a config file with telemetry enabled and
  an anonymous id, a 199M cache with its own headless browser, and preview logs, all under
  the home directory. The agent set `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and
  skipped the usage beacons the skill asks for. Four help calls ran before the opt-out.
- **Remotion's default render was untagged for colour.** The first render decoded the accent
  as `#43B589` instead of the briefed `#4CC38A`. The agent found `--color-space=bt709` in the
  CLI help and used it for the final. That flag is not in the skills. The skills-only render
  is described in the run log.
- **Both agents found their layout bugs only by rendering stills and looking.** HyperFrames:
  a data line readable for about 1.3 s, labels too small at phone width. Remotion: an accent
  bar that had shrunk to nothing, and non-opaque pixels during slides.
- **Each skill shaped the result in a visible way.** HyperFrames' motion rules produced four
  different entrances and three kinds of seam. Remotion's `TransitionSeries` rule produced
  overlapping transitions with no empty frame at a cut.
- **The HyperFrames clip counts up to 147**, so it shows numbers that are not in the brief
  (54, 112) on the way. For a line that reports a verification result, that is a defect.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
text:
- One run per arm. A second run could reverse any difference here.
- The agent under test was a Claude subagent, not an interactive Claude Code session, and
  it could not open a live preview.
- The HyperFrames arm used the skills bundled in the npm package, not the ones the installer
  fetches. They were not compared.
- The reviewer's brief names both toolchains, so it knew which two stacks were compared,
  though not which clip was which.
- The brief is ambiguous on whether "Step 1" is on-screen copy. Each arm read it differently
  and each lost a point for copy.
- Wall time, render counts and fix counts come from the agents' logs.
- Not measured: token cost, repeatability, audio, motion at playback speed.
